unresolved.reason: Client callability or an equivalent retained client mapping has not been established; remains required pending member-level review.

decisions.reason: Client region factory/shortcut contracts include LOCAL and persistent local variants; equivalent SPI configuration and behavior remain required.
Client cache construction, properties, PDX and default-pool settings remain required through injected typed assembly; native static factory shape is not prescribed.
Client interest-result selection and client pool socket creation remain required; these are not server interest observers or server subscription configuration.
Peer region factory/shortcut receiver is outside client-only creation; ClientRegionFactory/ClientRegionShortcut retain the client equivalents independently.
Peer cache/region construction is excluded; shared cache metadata, PDX and borrowed callback handles require separate review.
Server hosting, sessions, load probes and server-side registration observers are excluded; client pools, interest registration and subscription delivery remain separate requirements.
WAN sender/receiver, asynchronous queue and conflict-resolution hosting are excluded; shared event metadata and exceptions are not classified by package name.
Peer membership/role listener receivers require peer hosting; inherited listener methods stay required for client CacheListener receivers and must preserve their client tests.

Client listener/loader/writer hooks, event metadata and ordinary client transaction operations; descriptive enum values do not enable hosting. Native client tests and member-level disposition evidence apply.
Peer membership/roles, WAN payloads/configuration, hosting attributes/locks, network search, transaction writer and unsupported distributed transaction mode are outside the client-only contract.

Real LOCAL client transactions deliver commit, rollback and conflict outcomes; empty transactions also deliver outcomes. Server-backed client stub notification silence does not exclude locally hosted client callbacks.

Client listener registration and cleanup work on the native manager; both initialization hooks adapt a client cache and properties without extra lifecycle calls. Spring assembly and native-free mock support remain required.
Real client-local callbacks expose transaction identity, borrowed client cache and original/staged entry payloads; empty client transactions expose empty event lists.
Client ID/object submission, timed execution, arguments, region filters and collectors require typed equivalents; server-target filters retain native rejection.
Client submission consumes identity, result, HA and write-routing metadata; type scope does not settle body or permission callbacks.
Client execution propagates function failures, aggregate exceptions and cause/message diagnostics through typed equivalents.
Region, pool and client/authenticated-view targets require injected client equivalents, without a public native static service.
Client collectors require result and timed retrieval, member-tagged delivery, completion and retry clearing without stronger ordering guarantees.
Distributed-system member/group execution is outside client-only scope; client server-group routing remains a separate requirement.

Client registration retains function objects for local lookup and invocation metadata; preserve replacement, detached enumeration and native shared lifecycle through injected typed collaborators. It does not install server functions or establish remote availability or authorization.

Persistent local client regions execute function bodies with client-local contexts and result senders. Preserve typed callbacks, borrowed client cache/dataset access, invocation metadata and terminal result behavior without exposing server caches or peer hosting.

Map the protected FunctionService constructor and its internal service dependency to injected typed client execution collaborators. Preserve retained client service behavior without copying native inheritance, peer operations or static singleton assembly.

Client-submitted functions declare permissions evaluated by the remote execution command. Preserve DATA:WRITE defaults, region-only delegation and argument-aware overrides through typed native-free declarations; authorization remains on the server, without public server security management.

Client-submitted functions need native-free permission declarations, including component and wildcard construction with distinct observable fields and effective parts; preserve defaults, normalization and validation.
Client permission declarations use wildcard and NULL sentinels, including legacy region/key aliases. Preserve their values through typed equivalents without requiring old native names.
Client declaration equality, hashing and implication have distinct part-based semantics. Preserve them over native-free values without treating comparison as user authorization.
Client declaration inspection and rendering are observable separately from effective wildcard parts. Preserve the component values and region alias; rendering is not a transport encoding.

Client declaration extensions can inspect and edit effective wildcard parts independently of component fields. Preserve that behavior in an instance-owned typed representation, including nested aliases; no Shiro subclass contract is required.

The inherited overload compares client permission declarations with wildcard values. Retain comparison over typed wildcard parts; do not expose the Shiro Permission interface or add arbitrary authorization providers.
Client declaration extensions can replace effective parts without changing component fields. Preserve the pinned case-sensitive default and parser validation through typed declaration editing.

Client declaration extensions can explicitly choose case-sensitive or lowercasing parsing independently of component fields. Retain both modes through typed declaration editing, not a native superclass.

Client declaration extensions can supply pre-split ordered parts with subpart sets. Preserve effective structure and mutable alias behavior in the local typed editing model; snapshot both levels at transport boundaries.

Resource, operation and target enum values describe client-submitted function permissions. Preserve names, wildcard aliases, lookup and enumeration; CLUSTER/MANAGE/DISK/GATEWAY/DEPLOY labels do not expose server administration.

Pinned client query response construction and CQ initial-results contracts expose result collections, structs and typed metadata, including inherited collection operations; preserve through native-free equivalents with native mutability/failure behavior.

Pinned client query response construction and CQ initial-results contracts expose result collections, structs and typed metadata, including inherited collection operations; preserve through native-free equivalents with native mutability/failure behavior.

Pinned client/local/pool query paths support query construction, parameters, results, inspection, statistics and region query conveniences; preserve native unsupported compilation and distinct undefined results through typed equivalents.

Pinned client CQ creation, pool subscription, initial results, event/status dispatch, attribute mutation and statistics establish client behavior, including inherited callback defaults and declarative hooks; retain service-specific restrictions and native-free payloads.

Client-local query services support index definition, creation, inspection, removal and statistics; preserve local semantics and pool/authenticated-view restrictions without exposing remote index administration.

These two Query.execute overloads require a server region-function context and execute against local partition buckets; ordinary client query execution and client function submission remain required separately.

Client query responses carry serializable object/collection/struct metadata. Preserve encoding/decoding through typed equivalents and private versioned codecs, including nested type/field order and failures; do not export native DataSerializable inheritance.

Client regions expose map/bulk/local operations, entry and collection views, hierarchy, statistics, owner access and pool-backed server observations. Preserve typed native/mock behavior and explicit unavailable-operation failures; server inspection is not server hosting.

LocalRegion and Region defaults implement client key/regex/all-keys/iterable registration, unregister and list inspection through the pool, including policy, durable and receive-values flags and method-specific failures.

ClientRegionFactoryImpl.createSubregion invokes the native attribute-based Region overload. Preserve equivalent client-compatible attribute-copy creation and validation through typed configuration; shortcut-only creation does not prove equivalence.

Client callback and declarable contracts retain close, legacy init and distinct initialize hooks. Client XML invokes initialize then init; programmatic callback registration does not imply declarative initialization. Adapt Cache to a typed client owner.

GemFireCacheImpl exposes its transaction manager to clients; inherited Cache/GemFireCache/ClientCache access must preserve the connection-owned typed manager and existing verified client transaction behavior.

Pinned production source exposes EventSequenceID only through AsyncEvent and constructs it in GatewaySenderEventImpl. Retained client entry/CQ callbacks do not expose this server async/WAN payload; no current SPI or Spring consumer maps it.
GemFireCacheImpl and authenticated ProxyCache implement retained client cache/service access; the inherited Cache receiver does not require peer construction.
Client GemFireCacheImpl exposes disk/resource/snapshot, runtime/logging, query/JSON, authenticated-view and durable-ready collaborators; they are client service access, not server hosting.
CacheFactoryStatics lookup accepts an existing client cache and validates lifecycle/system identity; native version observation is also client-applicable despite the peer factory receiver.
ClientRegionFactoryImpl copies named attributes through InternalClientRegionAttributesFactory, while AttributesFactory and region attributes/mutators carry client-local settings and callbacks.
Legacy MirrorType and persist-backup convert data policies also used under LOCAL client scope; their client-local storage/persistence semantics remain applicable without peer replication.

Public EvictionAttributes.convertToConfigEvictionAttributes exposes these values from client eviction, and EvictionAttributesImpl.fromConfig consumes them; their client applicability is not inferred from schema membership alone.

PartitionAttributes DTO members and the protected bucket-region marker describe partition hosting, placement, recovery and server callbacks; clients route to server partitions without hosting this configuration.
Legacy enableConflation/enableBridgeConflation aliases configure server subscription queues, not the client pool subscription channel.
Peer locks/search, server HA-queue synchronization, membership discovery and distributed-system auto-rejoin do not describe client cache or pool runtime controls.
Inherited createGatewaySenderFactory on GemFireCache/ClientCache constructs WAN sender hosting infrastructure; approved client-only scope excludes that service despite interface reachability.
CacheFactory set, security-manager, post-processor and meter-subregistry setters configure the peer cache builder; client construction has separate ClientCacheFactory contracts.
DeclarableType.EMPTY is explicitly the gfsh alter-region declarable removal sentinel, not client initialization or nullable callback configuration.

Provide typed client region expiry/eviction/compression creation, readback and mutation with explicit-setting flags, shortcut validation, statistics/cloning constraints, reset policy, old-value returns and callback identity.

Provide native-free expiration actions, attributes and TTL reset values with constructor normalization, default/null distinctions, ordinal/XML parsing, equality/hash/string behavior and creation-time versus last-modified expiry semantics.
Provide native-free expiration binary hydration/serialization preserving timeout/action and hydration-versus-constructor differences; coordinate task 55 codecs without exposing native DataSerializer.

Provide typed entry-scoped CustomExpiry with nullable/default fallback, callback identity and replacement, inherited close/init/initialize contracts and explicit lifecycle ownership; preserve native exception handling without leaking Region.Entry or Cache.

Provide native-free eviction actions/algorithms, LRU/LIFO factories, defaults, sizing references and live maximum mutation; preserve inherited value/serialization behavior, equality excluding sizer, action-based isNoEviction and task 49 conversion precedence/failures.

Provide typed ObjectSizer callbacks and distinct reflection/class-once default strategies for client-local memory/heap eviction; preserve callback results and strategy differences without native sizing objects.

Provide native-free Compressor byte-array callbacks and Snappy-compatible construction/default/equality/failure behavior with client local-storage integration, cloning constraints and explicit mock capability; migrate Spring compression configuration.
Preserve typed pool settings and effective readback, omitted versus explicit values, native-version validation, configured endpoints, callback identity and Spring pool adapter/configuration adoption.

Retain observable pool defaults and sentinel semantics through native-free typed configuration and versioned driver defaults; preserve unset versus explicit false, zero, empty, negative sentinels and default socket selection.
Complete typed pool factory assembly, endpoint validation, reset/reuse, named creation and duplicate-name failure with driver-owned registration and native-free Spring consumers.
Preserve owned versus borrowed pool/cache close, keepAlive, attachment guards, destruction state, repeat-close behavior and native shutdown ordering; keep global native bookkeeping private.

Provide durable readiness and reconnect-time pending-event observations with subscription/durable prerequisites, pre-ready timing, negative sentinels and real queue replay/timeout acceptance; mock must reject unavailable remote effects.
Expose native-free live online-locator and current-server endpoint observations, distinct from configured endpoints, preserving empty results and snapshot semantics.

Preserve actual lazy default pool selection, reuse/compatibility, absent/ambiguous results, native localhost fallback and unique creation without hardcoding a pool name or introducing Spring native lookups.

Provide injected pool factory/lookup/enumeration/region association and owned close semantics, preserving absent lookup and snapshot behavior without public static registries or cross-context shutdown.

Retain typed client credential collection, mutable input/returned properties, initialization and close lifecycle, endpoint context and translated failures without native logger/member/cache types or peer authentication hosting.
Preserve username, password and token credential-key values independently of the excluded server SecurityManager interface; keep credential generation and failure handling client-side.

Replace native ConfigProperty and static JNDIInvoker exposure with typed client datasource name/value/type configuration and injected binding, preserving XML parsing, validation, binding failures and resource ownership.

Retain locator/server TLS channel selection and native all-channel interpretation for client transports, through native-free client configuration; do not expand public configuration to hosting/admin channels.

Exclude legacy AccessControl authorization hosting and its OperationContext/OperationCode payloads, including inherited initialization/close and operation classifiers; client callbacks/results use separate retained contracts.
Exclude Authenticator and all initialization/authenticate/close variants: they validate incoming credentials on the accepting server or locator, rather than collect credentials in the client.
Exclude SecurityManager hosting, initialization, authenticate, authorize and close; preserve its three credential-key constants separately and keep client-visible failure translation.
Exclude server PostProcessor initialization, value filtering and close: client receipt of processed values does not require hosting the server callback.
Exclude CLUSTER, GATEWAY, GRPC, JMX and WEB channel selectors from the public client configuration; these configure peer/WAN or server administrative/service endpoints.
Retain typed PDX/document values, schema/identity, writable copies, enum and factory behavior; task 58 owns unfinished transport and Serializable replacement, with Spring adoption downstream.
Retain typed PDX reader/writer/serializer callbacks and unread-field carriers, with missing/default/type behavior, decline semantics and versioned failure translation.
Retain shared client PDX configuration readback and metadata registration; explicitly distinguish accepted-but-ignored client persistence settings from supported disk persistence.
Exclude the five CacheFactory PDX setters on the peer-cache builder; retain ClientCacheFactory configuration and shared client PDX operations through their separately assigned equivalents.
Retain typed binary callbacks, serializer identities/classes and instantiator registration with collision, class-loading and propagation semantics; own native global registries privately.
Preserve internal registration event/context behavior privately in the native adapter; do not expose native event IDs, membership contexts or Object escape hatches in the SPI.
Retain binary framing/options/diagnostics privately through versioned codecs and typed per-call configuration; do not reproduce mutable global ThreadLocal state in the public SPI.
Retain client region reference serialization by full path with existing-cache resolution and missing/closed failures; inject a typed resolver rather than adding a static native cache lookup.
Retain typed binary helpers for primitives, boxed values, arrays, collections, maps, objects/classes and optionals, with null/kind/order/filter and checked-failure semantics in versioned codecs.
Retain injected serializer lookup/unregister behavior needed by client registration, including delayed class resolution and absent IDs; hide native static registry access.
Retain JSON document/factory and serialization interfaces with PDX/BSON storage selection, typed nested values and parser failures; keep external type-registry requirements version-owned.
Retain JSON/PDX conversion, identity options and client context through injected typed services; preserve or explicitly replace pinned text encoding and authenticated-context behavior.
Retain reflection serializer configuration, lifecycle and typed field/class/identity/transform hooks through client context; preserve selection, cache invalidation and callback failure behavior.
Retain reflection serializer manager behavior as a private implementation collaborator; do not expose AutoSerializableManager or an opaque Object manager in the SPI.
Retain typed PDX field-kind/default/width semantics, keeping versioned wire default bytes and mutable buffer position private rather than exposing native FieldType.
Retain typed client cancellation state, cause and close failures; hide native JVM failure machinery.
Retain durable ID, timeout and pool-qualified identity with explicit snapshot/alias semantics; do not expose native thread-local state.
Retain injected local client runtime identity, lifecycle and safe property/file configuration; keep native connection registries private.
Retain client-local statistics factories/lookups and logging through typed runtime services, coordinated with the statistics-family audit.
Exclude peer administration, membership discovery, auto-rejoin and thread-owned peer transport controls; retain independent client identity, pool recovery and sockets.
Exclude local locator construction, hosting, global lookup and stop APIs; retain client pool locator endpoints and discovery.
Exclude management declarable class-name/configuration DTOs; preserve independent client callback configuration and client XML parsing.
Retain verified client runtime/configuration keys with validation, aliases and safe readback, through typed client configuration.
Retain client-local logging, statistics and thread-monitor properties, including member-timeout used by client monitoring.
Retain client authentication initialization, DH exchange, security logging and property namespace; keep credentials out of diagnostics.
Retain modern client locator/server TLS and legacy cluster/server TLS fallback settings; preserve channel selection, defaults, validation and credential redaction.
Exclude TLS aliases/protocol settings used only by peer, gateway, gRPC, JMX or web hosting; preserve outbound locator/server TLS separately.

Exclude peer membership, multicast, transport, reconnect and distributed transaction settings; retain independent client pool transport and ordinary client transactions.
Exclude locator/server hosting, cluster deployment/configuration, management and REST administration properties; retain client XML and application classpath loading.
Retain client-local statistics metadata, factories, values, sampling callbacks and close semantics through typed runtime services.
Retain client and authentication logging levels, causes, tracing, localization and Java logging bridges without native logger interfaces in Spring.
Retain message identity, raw text, formatting and localized fallback through native-free values or private logging adaptation.

source_decisions.reason: Retain query failure translation and absent-class fallback; retire obsolete native reflection during client utility migration. No new native API or legacy-version support is implied.
Retain exclusion of provider infrastructure from application mapping through typed serialization integration; package strings are policy, not server hosting or class loading.
Retain useful client test logging configuration; remove or relocate native category settings with test-resource migration. Category names do not load native classes.
Remove stale CacheServer import/Javadoc during residual utility cleanup; documentation creates no client API or server hosting requirement.
Retain the client pool server endpoint default using a native-free constant; CacheServer receiver scope does not exclude the client endpoint value.
Retain the client server-port default used by endpoint parsing; replace native constant linkage without exposing CacheServer.
